root_cause.text: The MPTCP in-kernel path manager’s endpoint-removal logic in net/mptcp/pm_kernel.c inconsistently updated msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap, leaving some removed non-SUBFLOW endpoint IDs marked as still in use and causing later state corruption/assertions when the same ID was reused.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that after removing an endpoint “the corresponding bit in msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap was still unset,” because removal “only marked [the ID] as available for ‘signal’ types with an announced address, plus all ‘subflow’ types, but not the other types like an endpoint corresponding to the initial subflow”; the patch fixes this by moving __set_bit(addr->id, msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap) into the common removal path for all non-SUBFLOW endpoints.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop releasing the address ID bitmap entry during annotated address removal to prevent incorrect ID reuse while still updating removal bookkeeping.
intent_record.what: Inside mptcp_pm_remove_anno_addr(), the conditional block under `if (ret || force)` was changed so that when `ret` is true it no longer calls `__set_bit(addr->id, msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap);`, while it still decrements `msk->pm.add_addr_signaled--`; the surrounding braces were removed accordingly.
intent_record.how: At runtime, a failed or successful annotated address removal path that sets `ret` will no longer mark the address ID as available in `id_avail_bitmap`. This prevents the ID from being prematurely returned to the pool while still updating the count of signaled addresses and removing the address state, avoiding inconsistent ID reuse.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix address removal to atomically update PM state and release endpoint IDs for non-subflow endpoints as well as subflow endpoints.
intent_record.what: The code removes two separate spin_lock_bh/spin_unlock_bh sections around subflow removal and endpoint availability handling, replacing them with a single lock region. Inside that unified critical section, it still conditionally calls mptcp_pm_rm_subflow(msk, &list) when remove_subflow is true, still calls __mark_subflow_endp_available(msk, list.ids[0]) when the entry has MPTCP_PM_ADDR_FLAG_SUBFLOW, and newly adds an else branch that calls __set_bit(addr->id, msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap) for non-subflow endpoints.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this ensures endpoint ID availability updates happen atomically under the same pm lock as subflow removal, and it newly marks non-subflow endpoint IDs as available again when an address is removed. This prevents endpoint IDs such as signal or MPC endpoints from remaining unavailable after removal.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition is the core faulty logic: it limits endpoint-ID release handling to SUBFLOW endpoints only. As a result, removing a non-SUBFLOW endpoint does not clear its ID usage state in msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap, causing the inconsistent bitmap state described in the root cause.

This direct bitmap update during annotated address removal contributed to inconsistent PM state and incorrect ID reuse/bookkeeping mismatch. The fix intent explicitly removes this release here to avoid corrupting endpoint ID availability tracking.

commit 8617e85e04bd08c6c6aa24c832f9bec10bf76648
Author: Matthieu Baerts (NGI0) <matttbe@kernel.org>
Date:   Fri Mar 7 12:21:58 2025 +0100

    mptcp: pm: split in-kernel PM specific code
    
    Before this patch, the PM code was dispersed in different places:
    
    - pm.c had common code for all PMs
    
    - pm_netlink.c was supposed to be about the in-kernel PM, but also had
      exported common Netlink helpers, NL events for PM userspace daemons,
      etc. quite confusing.
    
    To
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet includes the full endpoint-removal path and the per-socket bitmap updates, so it is sufficient to judge. The vulnerable construct is present in `mptcp_nl_remove_subflow_and_signal_addr()`: after removing announced addresses and optionally removing subflows, it restores `msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap` only under `if (entry->flags & MPTCP_PM_ADDR_FLAG_SUBFLOW) { ... __mark_subflow_endp_available(msk, list.ids[0]); ... }`. That means bitmap restoration happens only for endpoints carrying the SUBFLOW flag. However, the root cause is specifically that removed non-SUBFLOW endpoint IDs can remain marked unavailable. This function also calls `mptcp_pm_remove_anno_addr(msk, addr, ...)`, and inside that helper the bitmap is restored only when `mptcp_remove_anno_list_by_saddr(msk, addr)` returns true: `if (ret) { __set_bit(addr->id, msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap); msk->pm.add_addr_signaled--; }`. So for a removed endpoint that is not SUBFLOW, if it is not currently in the anno list (or otherwise `ret` is false), there is no unconditional `__set_bit()` on deletion, leaving the ID unavailable. That is exactly the inconsistent update described by the vulnerability. There is no visible fix adding unconditional restoration for removed non-SUBFLOW endpoint IDs in the delete path; instead availability is still conditional on announcement removal success or on the SUBFLOW flag. Therefore the bug is present and the fix is not yet included.

Author: Matthieu Baerts (NGI0) <matttbe@kernel.org>

    mptcp: pm: split in-kernel PM specific code
    
    Before this patch, the PM code was dispersed in different places:
    
    - pm.c had common code for all PMs
    
    - pm_netlink.c was supposed to be about the in-kernel PM, but also had
      exported common Netlink helpers, NL events for PM userspace daemons,
      etc. quite confusing.
    
    To
bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant endpoint-removal logic is fully visible in this snippet, especially in `mptcp_nl_remove_subflow_and_signal_addr()` and the helper `__mark_subflow_endp_available()`, so the diff is sufficient to judge. The root cause is inconsistent updating of `msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap` when removing endpoints. In `mptcp_nl_remove_subflow_and_signal_addr()`, bitmap restoration is done only under `if (entry->flags & MPTCP_PM_ADDR_FLAG_SUBFLOW) { ... __mark_subflow_endp_available(msk, list.ids[0]); ... }`. That means for endpoints that are removed but do NOT have the `SUBFLOW` flag (e.g. non-SUBFLOW endpoints such as SIGNAL-only ones), this function does not set the ID back available in `msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap`. Yet those IDs are marked unavailable earlier when used, e.g. `mptcp_pm_create_subflow_or_signal_addr()` does `__clear_bit(local.addr.id, msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap);` both for signal addresses and for subflow creation. For signaled addresses, `mptcp_pm_remove_anno_addr()` only restores the bit when `mptcp_remove_anno_list_by_saddr(msk, addr)` returns true: `if (ret) { __set_bit(addr->id, msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap); msk->pm.add_addr_signaled--; }`. But `mptcp_nl_remove_subflow_and_signal_addr()` calls `mptcp_pm_remove_anno_addr(msk, addr, remove_subflow && !(entry->flags & MPTCP_PM_ADDR_FLAG_IMPLICIT));`, so if the announcement is no longer present (`ret == false`) and force is not triggered, the bit is not restored there either. As a result, removed non-SUBFLOW endpoint IDs can remain cleared/unavailable in `msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap`, matching the described vulnerability. There is no unconditional restoration of the removed endpoint ID on deletion, so the fix is not present.

bic_trace_step.reason: The provided function bodies are sufficient because the endpoint removal logic and bitmap updates are shown directly in this file. The vulnerable construct is present in `mptcp_nl_remove_subflow_and_signal_addr()`: after removing announced addresses and subflows, it only restores `msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap` when `entry->flags & MPTCP_PM_ADDR_FLAG_SUBFLOW` is set: `if (entry->flags & MPTCP_PM_ADDR_FLAG_SUBFLOW) { ... __mark_subflow_endp_available(msk, list.ids[0]); ... }`. For endpoints that are removed but do not have the `SUBFLOW` flag (e.g. SIGNAL-only/non-SUBFLOW endpoints), there is no corresponding `__set_bit(..., msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap)` or equivalent, so their ID can remain marked unavailable. The helper `mptcp_pm_remove_anno_addr()` does set the bit back only when `mptcp_remove_anno_list_by_saddr(msk, addr)` returns true: `if (ret) { __set_bit(addr->id, msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap); msk->pm.add_addr_signaled--; }`. That is inconsistent with the later unconditional SUBFLOW-path restoration and means non-SUBFLOW endpoint removal is not uniformly restoring the bitmap state. This matches the root cause: removed non-SUBFLOW endpoint IDs may stay marked as in use. Therefore the bug is present, and there is no fix here that ensures all removed endpoint IDs are made available again regardless of flags/state.
